name: Example: Applying the Second Fundamental Theorem of Calculus Using the Chain Rule
worked_solution:
To compute $f'(x),$  we first make the substitution $u=x^2$  and then we apply the chain rule, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}{\int }_{2}^{{x}^{2}}\operatorname{arctan}⁡t\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{\text{du}}{\text{d}x}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}{\int }_{2}^{u}\operatorname{arctan}⁡t\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

 

The integrand is continuous for all $t,$ so by FTC II we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\cdot \operatorname{arctan}⁡(u) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2})\cdot \operatorname{arctan}⁡(u) \\  & =2x\operatorname{arctan}⁡({x}^{2}).\end{aligned}
$$
